name: How are cooling, insulation, and humidity managed during a garage conversion?
description: Comfort is maintained by sealing exterior walls, installing continuous insulation and drywall, and adding an independent ductless mini-split HVAC system.

mainEntity.name: How are cooling, insulation, and humidity managed during a garage conversion?

acceptedAnswer.text: Garages are built as unconditioned utility zones, meaning their existing concrete slabs and exterior walls lack standard residential climate barriers. In the warm, humid climate of Hillsborough and Pinellas counties, standard air-handling systems rarely have the duct capacity to cool an extra 400 to 500 square feet. Successful conversions usually incorporate a ductless mini-split heat pump to provide independent, energy-efficient temperature and humidity control. Additionally, exterior block walls require rigid insulation, moisture vapor barriers, and quality drywall finishing to prevent condensation and keep the room comfortable year-round.
acceptedAnswer.description: Comfort is maintained by sealing exterior walls, installing continuous insulation and drywall, and adding an independent ductless mini-split HVAC system.
